findings: Library, not paper: the target's evidence says that because of the duplicate 'no module imports both'. That is not so. The root Causal.lean imports both Causal.LemmaKSC (:63) and Causal.LemmaKObstruction (:64), and it built at HEAD. Lean v4.31.0 accepts two modules that declare the same theorem with the same type and universe parameters (Lean/Environment.lean:2184-2210, subsumesInfo: 'We allow different modules to prove the same theorem'; the proof term is not compared). In the merged environment const2ModIdx keeps the first module (Causal.LemmaKSC), and the ConstantInfo, including the proof term, is the later module's (Causal.LemmaKObstruction's). So the build could not have caught the duplicate. It is visible only to a source grep or to a dump of two closures.
questions: Which copy to keep. Reading taken: Causal.LemmaKObstruction's (through weaklyLocallyCompactSpace_of_globallyHyperbolic, which moves with it). Three reasons. Its helper moves too. It is byte-identical to a HEAD block. It is the proof term the root environment already carried. LemmaKSC's copy (HEAD :120-127, a self-contained proof through mem_interior_iff_mem_nhds) was deleted, not moved.
labels.type_check: Before merging, each closure was dumped separately at HEAD (import Causal.LemmaKSC; import Causal.LemmaKObstruction). Both copies have type hash 3324761659, universe list [u] and the binder telescope M{},inst[],C{},inst[](T2Space),hT(),hG(). The value hashes differ: LemmaKSC 2586026344, LemmaKObstruction 3386744771. A probe importing both modules also shows that the types are equal: Lean's import accepts the pair only under Expr equality of the types (subsumesInfo).

labels.new: Causal/LevinTimeFunction.lean:535 `theorem GloballyHyperbolic.hasTimeFunction [T2Space M] [SecondCountableTopology M] (hG : C.GloballyHyperbolic) (hT : C.Tarentin) : C.HasTimeFunction`, in namespace Causal.Causality, variables {M : Type u} [TopologicalSpace M] {C : Causality M}. Its conclusion is exactly the library's Causality.HasTimeFunction (Causal/CurvesExtend.lean:516). Elaborated: ∀ {M : Type u} [TopologicalSpace M] {C : Causal.Causality M} [T2Space M] [SecondCountableTopology M], C.GloballyHyperbolic → C.Tarentin → C.HasTimeFunction. The proof is two tactic lines: obtain from exists_timeFunction_of_secondCountable hT hG (monotonicity dropped), then the anonymous constructor. It is written in tactic mode, so no auxiliary matcher is created (kb/0066), and it is the module's only new constant. Dot notation works: `hG.hasTimeFunction hT`, and `(hG.hasTimeFunction hT).curvesExtend` (probe).

Causal.LevinTimeFunction.content: 38 moved constants and the new wrapper, 39 in all. collectAxioms gives only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound for each of the 39. Hypotheses are ladder properties (Tarentin, GloballyHyperbolic) or standing typeclasses (T2Space, SecondCountableTopology). The abstract Levin.* lemmas carry NormalSpace, WeaklyLocallyCompactSpace, SigmaCompactSpace, T1Space and SecondCountableTopology on an abstract X with a closed preorder r. No statement mentions a metric. The docstring quotes def:category_topological_spacetimes (ETT.tex:255) and prop:GH_Jferme (ETT.tex:1178), marks no label, gives a hypothesis checklist, and in SCOPE says that HasTimeFunction is not defi:fonction_temps (ETT.tex:1028), what stayed behind, the merged duplicate, and why the mathlib import is there.
Causal.LevinTimeFunction.why_paracompact: Mathlib.Topology.Compactness.Paracompact is not needed by any proof. Without it the moved exists_timeFunction_of_secondCountable elaborated to a different proof term: value hash 4097358787 against 4138677269 at HEAD, with the same type. The difference was in the instance arguments only. In LevinUtility's HEAD closure, typeclass search reached NormalSpace and RegularSpace through paracompact_of_locallyCompact_sigmaCompact, T4Space.of_paracompactSpace_t2Space and T3Space.toRegularSpace. In the narrower closure it went through instRegularSpaceOfWeaklyLocallyCompactSpaceOfR1Space and T2Space.t1Space. Diagnosed by re-elaborating the HEAD proof text under a probe name: in an environment importing Causal.LemmaKSC it gives exactly 4138677269, in Causal.LevinTimeFunction's closure 4097358787, and with that mathlib module added 4138677269 again. Hence the import, which keeps the moved proof term identical. It is a mathlib module, so the layer is unchanged.
